tasks.short: Collect supply requests and check stock, decide what to order within budget, compare supplier prices, fill the order, check it, send it, and check deliveries.

steps.what: Staff request supplies through the request form
Residential advisor checks stock and collects supply requests: from e-mails today, from one list per building after the change
Residential advisor decides what to order within the budget
Residential advisor compares supplier prices on websites
Residential advisor orders supplies for facilities by filling the order form
Residential advisor checks the final order: items, quantities and prices match what was decided, and the supplier and delivery address are right
Residential advisor sends the checked order to the supplier: by e-mail today, by one release in the purchasing system after the change
Residential advisor checks deliveries against the order

tasks.design: Staff request supplies through a form that feeds one list per building in the university purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}), so requests are not collected from e-mails. The contract catalogue shows contract prices for about 70% of order lines, so the advisor compares prices only for the rest, and the order is built from the catalogue items. Once checked, the advisor releases the order to the supplier from the system. Deciding what to order and checking deliveries stay with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by e-mail and prices were compared site by site.
tasks.enabler_now: Purchasing systems hold contract catalogues and send orders.
tasks.still_hard: Special items outside the catalogue still need quotes.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which supplies run out in exam weeks.

evidence.claim: Purchasing systems can hold contract catalogues with prices and send orders to suppliers.

assumptions: Boundary: from supplies needed to the delivery checked; paying invoices is outside.
Input contract: contract catalogue kept by purchasing; fallback is supplier websites and e-mail.
Scenario: about 70% of order lines are in the contract catalogue.

The advisor checks every order. s1 keeps 60 because the stock check on the shelves stays and only collecting e-mails goes. s3 keeps 40 for the lines outside the catalogue. s4 keeps 50 because catalogue lines fill in and the rest is typed. s6 keeps 20 for the release. Staff time on the form (s0, share 1) is outside the advisor's savings.

incremental.description: Residential advisor handles requests filed in the wrong category.

approvals.approved_version: The order with items, quantities and prices exactly as checked by the advisor in s5, sent once from the purchasing system to the chosen supplier; any change needs a new check and release.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about half the lines are in the catalogue, so more prices are compared and typed (22.3); high: about 70% of lines from the catalogue as assumed (33.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect spending into a spreadsheet, review it against the budget and decide corrections, prepare next year's budget, and discuss it with the manager.

steps.what: Residential advisor collects spending from invoices and orders into a spreadsheet
Residential advisor oversees the departmental budget by reviewing spending and deciding corrections
Residential advisor prepares the next year's budget proposal
Residential advisor discusses the budget with the housing manager

tasks.design: A budget report from the finance system ({ERP}) shows spending per cost centre and category against the budget each month, so spending is not collected from invoices into a spreadsheet. The budget template opens with last year's actuals and occupancy figures. Reviewing spending, deciding corrections and discussing the budget stay with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Spending was gathered from invoices and orders by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Finance systems report spending per cost centre against budget.
tasks.still_hard: Costs booked to the wrong cost centre distort the report.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which activity to cut when money runs short.
tasks.altitude: The advisor reviews spending instead of compiling it.

evidence.claim: Finance systems can report spending per cost centre against budget.

assumptions: Boundary: from the month ended to the budget discussed; budget approval is outside.
Input contract: costs booked to the residence cost centre by finance; fallback is the spreadsheet.

Budget decisions stay with the advisor and manager. s1 keeps 30 for checking the report and chasing wrong bookings. s3 keeps 75 because only copying last year's actuals and occupancy goes; the proposal itself is still worked out by the advisor.
Finance staff's time does not change.

incremental.description: Residential advisor reports costs booked to the wrong cost centre.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many costs are booked to the wrong place, so the advisor rebuilds much of the list, and last year's figures need reworking (14.0); high: clean cost centre bookings (26.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect rooms and common areas, tell students what to fix, record results on the checklist, check the list of open items, and send reminders.

steps.what: Residential advisor inspects rooms and common areas to see that housekeeping work is done properly
Residential advisor supervises students' housekeeping work by telling them what to fix
Residential advisor records inspection results: on a paper checklist today, on a tablet checklist after the change
Residential advisor checks the list of open items before reminders: each item is still open and each reminder names the right student, room and item
Residential advisor sends reminders to students who have not fixed items: one e-mail each today, one release from the system after the change

tasks.design: The inspection checklist runs on a tablet in the residence management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) instead of paper; recording each result takes the same time. Open items form a list per student; once the advisor has checked it, the advisor releases the reminders to those students from the system instead of one e-mail each. Inspecting and talking with students stay with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checklists were on paper and reminders typed one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Residence management systems run inspection checklists and send reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Shared kitchens make it hard to say who should fix what.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a group of students to agree on a cleaning rota.

evidence.claim: Residence management systems can run inspection checklists on a tablet and send reminders to residents.
Photos in rooms must not show students or their belongings beyond the finding; residents' data need a lawful basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the inspection due to reminders sent; cleaning contracts are outside.
Input contract: rooms and checklists set up in the system; fallback is paper.
Inspections, telling students, recording results and checking the list keep their full time. s5 keeps 10 for the release; the reminders are not typed one by one.
The advisor checks the list before reminders go out.
research_questions: Are items fixed sooner after reminders?

incremental.description: Residential advisor updates checklists per building.

approvals.approved_version: The reminders per student exactly as checked by the advisor in s4, sent once from the residence management system to those students; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many open items need a personal note, so half the reminder time stays (4.5); high: standard reminders fit most items (8.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather the student's incidents and warnings, decide on cancellation with the housing manager, meet the student, write the cancellation letter, check it, send it, and update the contract records.

steps.what: Residential advisor gathers the student's incident reports and warnings
Residential advisor decides with the housing manager whether cancellation is justified
Residential advisor meets the student to explain the cancellation
Residential advisor writes the cancellation letter with reasons
Residential advisor checks the final cancellation letter: the reasons match the incidents on file and the decision, and the end date and the student's address are right
Residential advisor sends the checked letter to the student: by e-mail today, by one release from the system after the change
Residential advisor prepares the contract cancellation in the records: end date, room and reason; today also e-mails the housing office
Residential advisor checks the prepared cancellation: the right student, contract, end date and room, matching the letter sent
Residential advisor enters the checked cancellation, which ends the contract, frees the room and notifies the housing office

tasks.design: Incident reports and warnings are kept on the student's file in the residence management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the advisor does not gather them from folders and e-mails. The cancellation letter template fills the student, contract, end date and the listed incidents, and the advisor writes the reasons. Once checked, the advisor releases the letter to the student from the system. The advisor then prepares the cancellation, checks it, and enters it there; that ends the contract, frees the room and notifies the housing office, so no separate e-mail is needed. Deciding and meeting the student stay with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incidents sat in folders and e-mails; letters and contract changes were done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Residence management systems hold incidents and contracts per student.
tasks.still_hard: Cancellations are contested and must be well documented.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a student they must leave without making things worse.

evidence.claim: Residence management systems can hold incidents, warnings and contracts per student and fill letter templates.
A cancellation decision may not rest solely on automated processing.

assumptions: Boundary: from repeated breaches to the contract cancelled; appeals are outside.
Input contract: incidents recorded on the student's file; fallback is folders and e-mail.
The decision stays with the advisor and housing manager.

The advisor checks every letter and every cancellation. s1 keeps 50 because incidents are on the file but are still read. s4 keeps 70 because the template fills student, contract, dates and incidents; the advisor writes the reasons. s6 keeps 20 for the release. s7 keeps 40 because the housing office e-mail goes.
research_questions: Do cancellations hold up better when contested?

incremental.description: Residential advisor keeps the letter template in line with the housing rules.

approvals.approved_version: The cancellation letter exactly as checked by the advisor in s5, sent once from the residence management system to the student's address on file; any change needs a new check and release.

The cancellation of this student's contract with end date and room exactly as checked by the advisor in s7c, entered once in the residence management system, which notifies the housing office; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a contested case where many incidents sit in folders and the reasons need long writing (17.5); high: a clear case with a complete file (25.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The residential advisor keeps deciding orders, budget corrections and cancellations and talking with students; e-mailed requests, compiled spending, paper checklists and hand-made letters shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An advisor with more time with residents.
